analysis:
All three units are for CHANGELOG.md only: base_text excerpts at lines 1311-1801 and head_text at lines 1-222. The change is documentation. No executable code, config or schema was supplied, so I found no concrete security regression or new attack surface. The new head entries describe behaviors that touch the threat model, but I could not verify any of them against source:
- Provider build environment (head lines 3-6): a dev release defaults to the dev coordinator and does not fall back to production. This touches TB-002 and the coordinator trust assumptions. The wss URL and CDN override handling were not reviewed.
- Provider cache storage controls (head line 10): external cache volumes, UUID pinning, an encryption requirement and the rolling-day write ledger. T-041 already describes CacheVolume and the 20 GiB reserve, so this looks consistent with it.
- Member-only security clearance and Bedrock review (head lines 12-14, 74-82): a CI/review-policy change outside the runtime threat model.
- Autopilot daily earnings floor (head lines 41-51): reward and payout logic, including baselines, admin backfill and a funded pool. T-060 covers this area. Confirm it separately in the source passes.
- Account erasure and soft-delete (head lines 125-154): T-059 covers these.
- Withdrawal funding queue (head lines 70-72): TB-008.
- Machine-scoped Autopilot (head lines 57-62): TB-011 and A-016.
- Demanded prefix reuse and the typical MTP acceptance default (head lines 21-30, 93-97): T-041 and T-007. Sampled output becomes approximate by default; the changelog states this explicitly.
- Coordinator logging of personal data (head lines 160-162): reduces exposure.

The next pass should confirm that the changelog claims match the actual source changes in the other files of this PR. It should also confirm that T-041 and the TTL/cache posture are not modified without sign-off, and that the mutation-gate default (head line 130) is applied.
